Stage 6: GenAI SaaS

GenAI SaaS Foundation: APIs, Customization & Deployment

The Shared Blueprint Behind Every AI SaaS Product You Will Build

~45 min read | Foundation | From LLM to revenue-generating SaaS

Why This Lecture Exists

You have trained a Mini GPT-2 from scratch. You understand tokenization, attention, transformers, and backpropagation. You can generate text with your own model. That is a remarkable achievement — but it is not a product. Nobody will pay for a Python script running in a Jupyter notebook.

This lecture bridges the gap between “I have an LLM” and “I have a SaaS product generating revenue.” Over the next five projects, you will build five real, deployable AI-powered SaaS applications: image generation, video generation, text rewriting, plagiarism detection, and document intelligence. Every single one of them shares the same architectural foundation, the same deployment pipeline, and the same monetization strategy.

Before we build any of those, we need to lay that foundation. This lecture covers the four pillars every GenAI SaaS product rests on: architecture (how the pieces fit together), API integration (connecting to AI backends), customization (making it your own), and deployment (putting it on the internet for real users).

What you will learn: By the end of this lecture, you will have a complete, reusable project template, a universal AI provider class that works with 4 different backends, a deployment pipeline, and a business strategy. Every subsequent GenAI project will reference this lecture as its starting point.

Part 1: The GenAI SaaS Architecture

The Four-Layer Stack

Every SaaS application you will build in this course follows the same four-layer architecture. This is not arbitrary — it is the architecture used by virtually every modern web application, from small indie projects to billion-dollar companies. Understanding it once means understanding it forever.

The four layers are:

  1. Frontend (Static HTML/CSS/JS) — What the user sees and interacts with. Served as static files by the same server that runs the API. No React, no Vue, no build step. Just clean HTML with vanilla JavaScript that calls your API endpoints. This keeps things simple and deployment trivial.
  2. API Layer (FastAPI) — The brain of your application. Receives requests from the frontend, validates input, enforces billing limits, calls the AI backend, and returns structured responses. FastAPI gives us automatic OpenAPI documentation, type validation, async support, and incredible performance.
  3. AI Backend — The intelligence layer. This can be your own Mini GPT-2 model (loaded into memory and running inference locally), or a commercial API like OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude. Your API layer abstracts this completely — the frontend never knows or cares which AI is doing the work.
  4. Storage & State — Where persistent data lives. User accounts, billing records, generated outputs, usage logs. For our projects, we start with simple file-based storage and environment variables, graduating to databases as complexity grows.

Why FastAPI?

We chose FastAPI for every project in this course for five specific reasons:

  • Async by default: AI API calls are slow (often 1–10 seconds). FastAPI handles thousands of concurrent requests while waiting for AI responses, unlike Flask which blocks on each one.
  • Automatic documentation: Every endpoint you create automatically appears in an interactive Swagger UI at /docs. This is invaluable for testing and for showing clients what your API can do.
  • Type safety: Pydantic models validate every request and response. If a client sends invalid data, they get a clear error message before your code even runs.
  • Performance: FastAPI is one of the fastest Python web frameworks available, rivaling Node.js and Go for I/O-bound workloads.
  • Static file serving: FastAPI can serve your HTML frontend directly, meaning one server, one deployment, one URL. No need for a separate frontend hosting service.

The Shared Project Structure

Every GenAI project you build will follow this exact directory structure. Memorize it — you will use it five times:

my-saas/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py          # FastAPI app + routes
│   ├── config.py         # Settings & env vars
│   ├── billing.py        # Usage tracking & tiers
│   └── [domain].py       # Project-specific logic
├── static/
│   └── index.html        # Frontend UI
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
└── .env

The app/main.py file is the entry point. It creates the FastAPI application, sets up CORS (so browsers can call your API), mounts the static files directory, and defines all your API routes. The config.py file reads environment variables and provides a single Settings object that the rest of the app imports. The billing.py file tracks usage per API key and enforces rate limits. And the [domain].py file is where each project’s unique logic lives — image generation for PixelForge, text rewriting for ProseAI, and so on.

This separation of concerns means you can swap out the AI backend without touching the frontend, change billing tiers without touching the AI logic, or redesign the UI without touching anything server-side. It is a clean, professional architecture that scales from a side project to a real business.

Part 2: Connecting to LLM APIs

Four Ways to Add Intelligence

The most important decision in any AI SaaS product is: where does the intelligence come from? You have four options, each with different trade-offs in cost, quality, latency, and control. Our unified AIProvider class lets you switch between all four with a single environment variable.

Option A: Your Own Mini GPT-2

You built this model from scratch in Lectures 24–32b. Loading it for inference means loading the trained weights into memory and running the forward pass yourself. The advantage is zero API costs and complete control. The disadvantage is that your 124M-parameter model produces lower-quality output than commercial models with hundreds of billions of parameters. This option is perfect for learning, demos, and use cases where “good enough” text generation works (autocomplete, simple suggestions, template filling).

Option B: OpenAI API (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o)

OpenAI provides the most widely-used commercial LLM API. To use it, you need an API key from platform.openai.com, which requires a payment method on file. The key goes in your .env file as OPENAI_API_KEY. The core endpoint is chat/completions, which accepts a list of messages (system prompt + user message) and returns the model’s response. OpenAI also supports streaming, where tokens arrive one-by-one for a real-time typing effect in your UI.

API Key Security: Never commit API keys to Git. Never put them in your frontend JavaScript. Always load them from environment variables on the server side. Your .env file should be in .gitignore. If you accidentally commit a key, rotate it immediately.

Option C: Google Gemini API

Google’s Gemini API is available through Google AI Studio. It offers excellent performance at lower prices than OpenAI, with particularly strong multimodal capabilities (understanding images, audio, and video alongside text). The API key comes from aistudio.google.com and goes in your .env as GEMINI_API_KEY. The endpoint uses generateContent instead of chat/completions, but the concept is identical: send messages, get a response.

Option D: Anthropic Claude API

Anthropic’s Claude API is known for careful, nuanced responses and strong instruction-following. The API key comes from console.anthropic.com and goes in your .env as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Claude’s messages endpoint works similarly to OpenAI but separates the system prompt into its own parameter rather than including it as a message.

The Unified AIProvider Class

Rather than writing different code for each API, we create a single AIProvider class that abstracts the differences. You configure which provider to use via the AI_PROVIDER environment variable. The class exposes one method — generate(prompt, system_prompt) — that works identically regardless of which backend is active. This means switching from your own model to GPT-4o to Gemini requires changing one environment variable and zero lines of application code.

Cost Comparison

Understanding costs is critical for building a profitable SaaS. Here are approximate costs per 1 million tokens (roughly 750,000 words) for the most cost-effective model in each provider’s lineup:

Provider Model Input Cost Output Cost Best For
Own Model Mini GPT-2 $0 (compute only) $0 Learning, demos
OpenAI GPT-4o-mini $0.15 $0.60 General-purpose
Google Gemini Flash $0.075 $0.30 Cost-sensitive, multimodal
Anthropic Claude Haiku $0.25 $1.25 Nuanced, instruction-following

For most student projects, GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash offer the best balance of quality and cost. You can start with your own model for development, then switch to a commercial API when you are ready to serve real users.

Part 2b: Authentication & User Management

You have connected your application to an LLM API. It can generate text, images, or analyze documents. But right now, anyone who finds your URL can use it — and every API call costs you money. Before your SaaS product can generate revenue, you need to know who is using it, how much they are using it, and whether they have paid for it. That is what authentication and user management solve.

Why Authentication Matters for SaaS Products

Authentication is not just a security feature — it is the foundation of your entire business model. Without it, you cannot:

  • Track usage per user: You need to know which user made which API call to enforce billing tiers and rate limits.
  • Charge for your service: Payment processing requires a user identity to associate with a subscription or payment method.
  • Protect your API keys: Without auth, your expensive OpenAI or Gemini API keys are effectively public. One malicious user could rack up thousands of dollars in charges.
  • Provide personalized experiences: Saved preferences, history, and custom settings all require a user account.
  • Comply with regulations: GDPR and other privacy laws require you to know whose data you are processing and provide them with control over it.

JWT-Based Authentication

All five GenAI SaaS products in this course use JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for authentication. Here is how it works:

  1. Login: The user sends their email and password to your /api/auth/login endpoint.
  2. Verification: Your server checks the credentials against the database.
  3. Token generation: If valid, the server creates a JWT — a cryptographically signed string containing the user ID, email, role, and expiration time.
  4. Client storage: The frontend stores this token (typically in an HTTP-only cookie or localStorage).
  5. Subsequent requests: Every API call includes the token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header.
  6. Validation: The server verifies the token signature on each request without hitting the database, making it extremely fast.

JWTs are stateless — the server does not need to store session data. This makes them perfect for distributed applications where multiple server instances handle requests. The token itself contains all the information needed to identify the user.

OAuth2 Social Login

Nobody wants to create yet another username and password. OAuth2 social login lets users sign in with accounts they already have. The two most common providers for developer tools and SaaS products are:

  • Google OAuth: Users click “Sign in with Google,” get redirected to Google’s login page, authorize your app, and are sent back with an authorization code. Your server exchanges this code for user profile information (name, email, avatar). This is the most widely accepted social login for professional tools.
  • GitHub OAuth: Same flow as Google but using GitHub accounts. Particularly popular for developer-focused tools. Many of your potential users already have GitHub accounts from the earlier lectures in this course.

In both cases, you never see or store the user’s password. The identity provider (Google or GitHub) handles all password management, two-factor authentication, and account recovery. You just receive a verified email address and profile data.

Auth Provider Comparison

You do not have to build authentication from scratch. Several services provide drop-in authentication with minimal code. Here is how they compare:

Provider Free Tier Pricing Best For Integration Effort
Clerk 10,000 MAU $25/month (Pro) Beautiful pre-built UI components, fastest setup Low — drop-in React/JS components
Auth0 7,500 MAU $23/month (Essentials) Enterprise features, extensive customization Medium — SDK integration, rule engine
Supabase Auth 50,000 MAU Included with Supabase ($25/month Pro) Already using Supabase for database, generous free tier Low — built into Supabase client library
Firebase Auth Unlimited (most features) Free for auth, pay for other Firebase services Google ecosystem, mobile apps, unlimited free auth Low — well-documented SDKs

For the SaaS projects in this course, Supabase Auth is the recommended choice if you are already using Supabase for your database, and Clerk is recommended if you want the fastest possible setup with the best-looking login pages out of the box.

How the SaaS Products Implement Auth

In each GenAI SaaS project, authentication is handled by two key files:

  • app/auth.py — Contains the authentication middleware, JWT token creation and validation, password hashing with bcrypt, and user session management. This file provides the get_current_user dependency that you add to any FastAPI endpoint that requires authentication. Protected endpoints automatically reject requests without a valid token.
  • app/stripe_checkout.py — Handles the connection between authentication and payments. When a user subscribes, Stripe sends a webhook to your server. This file processes that webhook, updates the user’s subscription status in the database, and adjusts their billing tier accordingly. The authenticated user ID links their Stripe customer record to their application account.

Rate Limiting and API Key Management

Authentication alone is not enough — you also need to control how much each user can consume. Rate limiting protects both your budget and your service quality:

  • Per-user rate limits: Free tier users might get 10 requests per day, while Pro users get 500. The billing.py module tracks usage per authenticated user and returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) when limits are exceeded.
  • API key management: For users who want programmatic access (calling your API from their own code), generate unique API keys tied to their account. Store keys as hashed values in your database, never in plaintext. Provide a dashboard where users can create, rotate, and revoke their API keys.
  • Global rate limiting: Beyond per-user limits, implement global rate limiting to prevent your entire service from being overwhelmed. Tools like Redis or simple in-memory counters can throttle total requests per second across all users.
  • Cost tracking: Log every API call with its token cost. This data feeds into your billing system and helps you set pricing that covers your AI API expenses with healthy margins.
Security reminder: Never expose your AI provider API keys (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) to the frontend. All AI API calls must go through your FastAPI backend, which adds the API key server-side. The user authenticates with your service; your service authenticates with the AI provider. Two separate authentication layers, each protecting different credentials.

Part 3: How to Customize Your SaaS

Making Each Project Your Own

The projects in this course are deliberately generic. “Text Rewriting SaaS” could be anything — a legal document tool, a marketing copy assistant, an academic paper editor, a social media post optimizer. The magic is in the customization. Here is your step-by-step guide to transforming any generic project into a specialized, marketable product.

Step 1: Branding

Open static/index.html and change everything visual. Replace the app name (“ProseAI” becomes “LegalDraft Pro”). Change the color scheme to match your target industry (navy blue and gold for legal, green for medical, bright colors for marketing). Add your logo. Update the tagline from generic (“Rewrite any text with AI”) to specific (“Transform legal briefs into winning arguments in seconds”). First impressions matter enormously — a well-branded tool feels professional and trustworthy.

Step 2: System Prompts

This is where the real differentiation happens. The system prompt tells the AI who it is and how to behave. A generic rewriting prompt like “You are a helpful text rewriting assistant” becomes “You are LegalDraft Pro, an expert legal writing assistant. You specialize in transforming rough legal drafts into polished, court-ready documents. You use precise legal terminology, maintain proper citation formats (Bluebook style), and ensure arguments follow a clear logical structure. You never fabricate case citations.” The same underlying AI becomes a completely different product just by changing the system prompt.

Step 3: Features & Endpoints

Each project comes with a set of API endpoints. Add the ones your niche needs and remove the ones it does not. A legal tool might add a “citation check” endpoint that validates legal references. A marketing tool might add a “generate variations” endpoint that produces 5 different versions of the same copy. Think about what workflow your target users follow and build endpoints that match each step.

Step 4: Billing Tiers

Customize the billing tiers for your market. A tool for solo lawyers might have: Free (5 rewrites/day), Professional ($29/month, 100 rewrites/day), and Firm ($99/month, unlimited + priority). A tool for marketing agencies might have completely different tiers based on team size and API access. The billing system is configuration-driven — change the numbers in config.py and the enforcement logic in billing.py handles the rest.

Step 5: Domain-Specific Vocabulary & White-Labeling

Add industry-specific terminology to your UI, error messages, and documentation. Legal users expect “briefs” and “motions,” not “documents” and “texts.” Medical users expect “patient records” and “clinical notes.” Finally, serve the application under your own domain name. A tool at legaldraftpro.com feels like a real product; a tool at my-app.railway.app feels like a student project.

Customization is not optional: The projects in this course are starting points, not finished products. Students who deploy them as-is will compete with thousands of other generic AI tools. Students who customize for a specific niche — who deeply understand their target users — will build something people actually pay for.

Part 4: Step-by-Step Deployment Guide

Getting Your App Online

A SaaS product that only runs on localhost:8000 is not a SaaS product. Deployment is the process of putting your application on a server that is accessible from anywhere in the world, 24/7. This section gives you three deployment options, from simplest to most flexible.

Prerequisites Checklist

Before deploying anything, verify these items:

  • Your application runs correctly with uvicorn app.main:app --reload locally
  • Your .env file has all required variables configured
  • Your Dockerfile builds and runs successfully with docker build -t myapp . && docker run -p 8000:8000 myapp
  • Your requirements.txt includes all dependencies with pinned versions
  • You have tested all API endpoints using the /docs Swagger UI
  • Your .gitignore excludes .env, __pycache__, and any large model files

Option A: Railway (Recommended for Beginners)

Railway is the simplest way to deploy a FastAPI application. It detects your Dockerfile automatically, provisions a server, and gives you a public URL in under 5 minutes. The free tier gives you $5/month in credits, which is enough for development and light usage.

The deployment process is straightforward: install the Railway CLI, authenticate with railway login, initialize your project with railway init, and deploy with railway up. Set your environment variables (API keys, settings) in the Railway dashboard. Railway automatically assigns a .railway.app subdomain, and you can configure a custom domain in the settings panel.

Option B: Render

Render connects directly to your GitHub repository and deploys automatically every time you push. This is ideal if you want continuous deployment — push code, and it is live within minutes. Create a render.yaml file in your project root to configure the service type, build command, start command, and environment variables. Render’s free tier spins down after 15 minutes of inactivity (cold starts take 30–60 seconds), so it is better for demos than production.

Option C: Split Architecture (Vercel + Railway)

For maximum performance, you can split your application: serve the static frontend from Vercel (which has a generous free tier and a global CDN) and run the FastAPI backend on Railway. This requires configuring CORS headers on your FastAPI app to allow requests from your Vercel domain, and updating your frontend JavaScript to call the Railway API URL instead of relative paths. This architecture is more complex but gives you the best of both worlds: fast static file delivery and a dedicated API server.

Post-Deployment Checklist

After your app is live, verify these critical items:

  • HTTPS: Both Railway and Render provide SSL certificates automatically. Verify by checking for the lock icon in your browser.
  • Environment variables: Confirm all secrets are set in the platform dashboard, not hardcoded in your code.
  • Health check: Your /health endpoint should return 200. Set up an uptime monitor (UptimeRobot, free tier) to alert you when it goes down.
  • Error tracking: Check your deployment logs for any startup errors or runtime exceptions.
  • Performance: Test your API response time from a different network. AI API calls should complete in 1–5 seconds for a good user experience.

Part 5: From Side Project to Real Business

Monetization Strategy

Building a great product is only half the battle. The other half is getting people to pay for it. This section covers the business fundamentals that turn a side project into a revenue-generating SaaS.

Payment Processing with Stripe

Stripe is the industry standard for SaaS payments. Integration involves three steps: creating a Stripe account, setting up Products and Prices in the Stripe dashboard (matching your billing tiers), and adding Stripe Checkout or Payment Links to your application. For your first version, Stripe Payment Links are the simplest option — you create a payment link in the Stripe dashboard and redirect users to it. No server-side Stripe code required. As you grow, you can integrate the full Stripe API for subscriptions, invoicing, and usage-based billing.

Analytics & Usage Tracking

You cannot improve what you do not measure. Add Google Analytics or Plausible (privacy-focused alternative) to your frontend to track visitor behavior: how many people visit, which pages they view, where they drop off. On the backend, log every API call with timestamps, user IDs, and response times. This data tells you which features people actually use and where your product needs improvement.

Pricing Strategy

The four-tier pricing model works for almost every SaaS product:

  • Free Tier (the hook): Limited usage (5–10 requests/day). No credit card required. Lets people experience your product before committing. This is your marketing funnel.
  • Starter ($9–19/month): Enough for individual users. 100–500 requests/day. Basic features. This is where most users start paying.
  • Pro ($29–79/month): For power users and small teams. Higher limits, premium features (faster models, priority processing, API access). This is your revenue driver.
  • Enterprise (custom pricing): For organizations with specific needs. Custom integrations, SLAs, dedicated support. Handle these through direct sales conversations.

Marketing Your AI SaaS

The best marketing channels for indie AI SaaS products are:

  • Product Hunt: Launch your product here for a burst of initial traffic and feedback. Prepare a compelling description, screenshots, and a demo video.
  • Indie Hackers / Hacker News: Share your building journey. “I built an AI legal writing tool in 2 weeks” gets attention and feedback.
  • Twitter/X and LinkedIn: Post demos, share insights about your niche, engage with potential users. Short video demos of your tool in action perform exceptionally well.
  • SEO & Content Marketing: Write blog posts about the problems your tool solves. “How to write a legal brief in half the time” attracts people searching for exactly what you offer.
  • Reddit: Find subreddits relevant to your niche (r/lawyers, r/marketing, r/writing) and genuinely help people. Mention your tool when relevant, not as spam.

Legal Requirements

Every SaaS product needs at minimum: a Terms of Service (what users agree to by using your product), a Privacy Policy (what data you collect and how you use it), and GDPR compliance if you serve European users (right to data deletion, cookie consent, data processing agreements). Use services like Termly or iubenda to generate these documents — do not skip them.

Part 6: What You Will Build Next

Five GenAI SaaS Projects

With this foundation in place, you are ready to build. Each of the following five projects is a complete, deployable SaaS product. They all use the shared architecture, the unified AI provider, and the deployment pipeline you learned in this lecture.

Project 1: Image Generation — PixelForge

A text-to-image SaaS with style controls. Users type a description (“a sunset over mountains in watercolor style”) and get a generated image. Features include style presets (photorealistic, anime, oil painting, pixel art), resolution options, and image-to-image variation. Uses DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, or your own diffusion model as the backend. Monetization is straightforward: charge per image generated.

Project 2: Video Generation — ClipCraft

A text-to-video and image-to-video SaaS. Users provide a text prompt or an image, and get a short video clip. This project introduces asynchronous processing — video generation takes minutes, not seconds, so you will build a job queue with status polling. Users submit a request, get a job ID, and check back for results. This is a common pattern in production AI applications.

Project 3: Text Composition & Rewriting — ProseAI

A text manipulation SaaS that can rewrite, summarize, expand, change tone, and translate text. This is the most customizable project — with the right system prompts, it becomes a legal writing tool, a marketing copy generator, an academic paper editor, or a creative writing assistant. Features include tone selection (formal, casual, persuasive, technical), length control, and multi-language support.

Project 4: Plagiarism & AI Detection — TruthLens

A content authenticity SaaS that detects both copied text (plagiarism) and AI-generated content. This project is more technically interesting than it appears — AI detection involves statistical analysis of text patterns (perplexity, burstiness, token probability distributions) alongside traditional plagiarism detection (n-gram matching, web search comparison). The market for this tool is enormous: educators, publishers, hiring managers, and content platforms all need it.

Project 5: OCR & Document Intelligence — DocMind

A document processing SaaS that extracts text, tables, and structured data from images and PDFs. Users upload a photo of a receipt, a scanned contract, or a handwritten note, and get structured, searchable text back. Advanced features include table extraction (preserving rows and columns), form field detection, and data extraction with AI (parsing invoices into line items, amounts, and dates). This project combines computer vision (OCR) with LLM intelligence (understanding what the extracted text means).

Choose Your Path

You can build all five projects to get broad experience across different AI modalities. Or you can pick the one or two that match your market opportunity and go deep — customizing, polishing, and launching them as real products. Either way, the foundation is the same, and it starts right here.

Ready to build? The code blocks below give you everything you need to get started: a complete project template, a universal AI provider, a customization example, a deployment script, an environment configuration template, and a landing page template. Copy them, customize them, and ship your first GenAI SaaS product.

Etapa 6: GenAI SaaS

Fundatia GenAI SaaS: API-uri, Personalizare si Deployment

Planul Comun din Spatele Fiecarui Produs AI SaaS pe Care il Vei Construi

~45 min lectura | Fundament | De la LLM la SaaS care genereaza venituri

De Ce Exista Aceasta Lectie

Ai antrenat un Mini GPT-2 de la zero. Intelegi tokenizarea, atentia, transformerele si backpropagation. Poti genera text cu propriul model. Aceasta este o realizare remarcabila — dar nu este un produs. Nimeni nu va plati pentru un script Python care ruleaza intr-un notebook Jupyter.

Aceasta lectie face puntea intre „Am un LLM” si „Am un produs SaaS care genereaza venituri.” In urmatoarele cinci proiecte, vei construi cinci aplicatii SaaS reale, deployabile, alimentate de AI: generare de imagini, generare de video, rescriere de text, detectie de plagiat si inteligenta documentelor. Fiecare dintre ele partajeaza aceeasi fundatie arhitecturala, acelasi pipeline de deployment si aceeasi strategie de monetizare.

Inainte sa construim oricare dintre acestea, trebuie sa punem aceasta fundatie. Aceasta lectie acopera cei patru piloni pe care se sprijina fiecare produs GenAI SaaS: arhitectura, integrare API, personalizare si deployment.

Partea 1: Arhitectura GenAI SaaS

Stiva cu Patru Straturi

Fiecare aplicatie SaaS pe care o vei construi in acest curs urmeaza aceeasi arhitectura cu patru straturi:

  1. Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS static) — Ce vede si cu ce interactioneaza utilizatorul. Servit ca fisiere statice de acelasi server care ruleaza API-ul.
  2. Stratul API (FastAPI) — Creierul aplicatiei tale. Primeste cereri, valideaza input, aplica limitele de facturare, apeleaza backend-ul AI si returneaza raspunsuri structurate.
  3. Backend AI — Stratul de inteligenta. Poate fi propriul tau model Mini GPT-2 sau un API comercial precum OpenAI, Google Gemini sau Anthropic Claude.
  4. Stocare & Stare — Unde traiesc datele persistente. Conturi de utilizator, inregistrari de facturare, output-uri generate, jurnale de utilizare.

De Ce FastAPI?

Am ales FastAPI pentru fiecare proiect din acest curs din cinci motive specifice: async implicit, documentatie automata, siguranta tipurilor, performanta si servirea fisierelor statice. FastAPI gestioneaza mii de cereri concurente in timp ce asteapta raspunsuri AI, spre deosebire de Flask care blocheaza la fiecare.

Structura Proiectului Partajat

my-saas/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py          # Aplicatia FastAPI + rute
│   ├── config.py         # Setari & variabile de mediu
│   ├── billing.py        # Urmarirea utilizarii & niveluri
│   └── [domain].py       # Logica specifica proiectului
├── static/
│   └── index.html        # Interfata frontend
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
└── .env

Partea 2: Conectarea la API-urile LLM

Patru Modalitati de a Adauga Inteligenta

Cea mai importanta decizie in orice produs AI SaaS este: de unde vine inteligenta? Ai patru optiuni:

  • Optiunea A: Propriul tau Mini GPT-2 — Zero costuri API, control complet, dar calitate mai scazuta.
  • Optiunea B: OpenAI API (GPT-4o-mini) — Cel mai utilizat API comercial. Cost: ~$0.15/1M tokens input.
  • Optiunea C: Google Gemini API — Performanta excelenta la preturi mai mici. Cost: ~$0.075/1M tokens input.
  • Optiunea D: Anthropic Claude API — Raspunsuri nuantate, urmarire excelenta a instructiunilor. Cost: ~$0.25/1M tokens input.

Clasa noastra unificata AIProvider abstractizeaza diferentele. Configurezi care furnizor sa fie folosit prin variabila de mediu AI_PROVIDER. Schimbarea de la propriul model la GPT-4o la Gemini necesita modificarea unei singure variabile de mediu si zero linii de cod al aplicatiei.

Securitatea Cheilor API: Nu comite niciodata chei API in Git. Nu le pune in JavaScript-ul frontend. Incarca-le intotdeauna din variabile de mediu pe server. Fisierul .env trebuie sa fie in .gitignore.

Partea 2b: Autentificare si Managementul Utilizatorilor

Ai conectat aplicatia la un API LLM. Poate genera text, imagini sau analiza documente. Dar in acest moment, oricine gaseste URL-ul tau o poate folosi — si fiecare apel API te costa bani. Inainte ca produsul tau SaaS sa poata genera venituri, trebuie sa stii cine il foloseste, cat de mult il foloseste si daca a platit pentru el. Asta rezolva autentificarea si managementul utilizatorilor.

De Ce Conteaza Autentificarea pentru Produsele SaaS

Autentificarea nu este doar o functionalitate de securitate — este fundatia intregului tau model de afaceri. Fara ea, nu poti:

  • Urmari utilizarea per utilizator: Trebuie sa stii care utilizator a facut care apel API pentru a aplica nivelurile de facturare si limitele de rata.
  • Percepe plata pentru serviciul tau: Procesarea platilor necesita o identitate de utilizator asociata cu un abonament sau o metoda de plata.
  • Proteja cheile tale API: Fara autentificare, cheile tale scumpe OpenAI sau Gemini sunt efectiv publice. Un utilizator rau-intentionat ar putea acumula mii de dolari in costuri.
  • Oferi experiente personalizate: Preferinte salvate, istoric si setari personalizate necesita toate un cont de utilizator.
  • Respecta reglementarile: GDPR si alte legi de confidentialitate iti cer sa stii ale cui date le procesezi.

Autentificare Bazata pe JWT

Toate cele cinci produse GenAI SaaS din acest curs folosesc JSON Web Tokens (JWT) pentru autentificare. Iata cum functioneaza:

  1. Login: Utilizatorul trimite emailul si parola la endpoint-ul /api/auth/login.
  2. Verificare: Serverul verifica credentialele in baza de date.
  3. Generare token: Daca sunt valide, serverul creeaza un JWT — un sir criptografic semnat care contine ID-ul utilizatorului, emailul, rolul si timpul de expirare.
  4. Stocare client: Frontend-ul stocheaza acest token (de obicei intr-un cookie HTTP-only sau localStorage).
  5. Cereri ulterioare: Fiecare apel API include tokenul in headerul Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  6. Validare: Serverul verifica semnatura tokenului la fiecare cerere fara a accesa baza de date, facandu-l extrem de rapid.

OAuth2 Login Social

Nimeni nu vrea sa creeze inca un nume de utilizator si o parola. OAuth2 social login le permite utilizatorilor sa se autentifice cu conturi pe care le au deja:

  • Google OAuth: Utilizatorii apasa „Autentificare cu Google”, sunt redirectionati la pagina de login Google, autorizeaza aplicatia ta si sunt trimisi inapoi cu un cod de autorizare. Serverul tau schimba acest cod pentru informatii de profil (nume, email, avatar).
  • GitHub OAuth: Acelasi flux ca Google dar folosind conturi GitHub. Deosebit de popular pentru instrumentele orientate catre dezvoltatori.

Comparatie Furnizori de Autentificare

Furnizor Nivel Gratuit Preturi Cel Mai Bun Pentru
Clerk 10.000 MAU $25/luna (Pro) Componente UI pre-construite frumoase, configurare rapida
Auth0 7.500 MAU $23/luna (Essentials) Functionalitati enterprise, personalizare extensiva
Supabase Auth 50.000 MAU Inclus cu Supabase ($25/luna Pro) Deja folosesti Supabase pentru baza de date, nivel gratuit generos
Firebase Auth Nelimitat (majoritatea functiilor) Gratuit pentru autentificare Ecosistemul Google, aplicatii mobile

Cum Implementeaza Produsele SaaS Autentificarea

In fiecare proiect GenAI SaaS, autentificarea este gestionata de doua fisiere cheie:

  • app/auth.py — Contine middleware-ul de autentificare, crearea si validarea tokenurilor JWT, hashingul parolelor cu bcrypt si managementul sesiunilor. Ofera dependenta get_current_user pe care o adaugi la orice endpoint FastAPI care necesita autentificare.
  • app/stripe_checkout.py — Gestioneaza conexiunea dintre autentificare si plati. Cand un utilizator se aboneaza, Stripe trimite un webhook catre serverul tau. Acest fisier proceseaza webhook-ul, actualizeaza statusul abonamentului si ajusteaza nivelul de facturare.

Rate Limiting si Managementul Cheilor API

Autentificarea singura nu este suficienta — trebuie sa controlezi cat poate consuma fiecare utilizator:

  • Limite per utilizator: Utilizatorii gratuit pot primi 10 cereri pe zi, in timp ce utilizatorii Pro primesc 500. Modulul billing.py urmareste utilizarea per utilizator autentificat.
  • Managementul cheilor API: Pentru utilizatorii care doresc acces programatic, genereaza chei API unice legate de contul lor. Stocheaza cheile ca valori hash in baza de date, niciodata in text clar.
  • Rate limiting global: Dincolo de limitele per utilizator, implementeaza limitarea globala a ratei pentru a preveni suprasolicitarea intregului serviciu.
  • Urmarirea costurilor: Logheaza fiecare apel API cu costul sau in tokeni. Aceste date alimenteaza sistemul de facturare si te ajuta sa stabilesti preturi care iti acopera cheltuielile cu API-ul AI.
Memento de securitate: Nu expune niciodata cheile API ale furnizorului AI (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) catre frontend. Toate apelurile API AI trebuie sa treaca prin backend-ul tau FastAPI, care adauga cheia API pe partea de server. Utilizatorul se autentifica cu serviciul tau; serviciul tau se autentifica cu furnizorul AI. Doua straturi separate de autentificare, fiecare protejand credentiale diferite.

Partea 3: Cum sa Personalizezi SaaS-ul Tau

Ghid Pas cu Pas

Proiectele din acest curs sunt deliberat generice. Magia sta in personalizare:

  1. Branding: Schimba numele aplicatiei, culorile, logo-ul in index.html.
  2. Prompts de Sistem: Modifica prompt-urile de sistem pentru a se potrivi nisei tale. Un prompt generic devine unul specific industriei.
  3. Functionalitati: Adauga/elimina endpoint-uri, schimba nivelurile de facturare.
  4. Focus pe Domeniu: Specializeaza-te pentru un vertical (legal, medical, educatie, marketing).
  5. White-labeling: Serveste sub propriul tau domeniu.

Exemplu: Transformarea genericului „SaaS de Rescriere Text” in „LegalDraft Pro” — un instrument de rescriere a documentelor juridice. Schimbi 5 lucruri: numele aplicatiei, prompt-ul de sistem, nivelurile de facturare, vocabularul specific domeniului si textul paginii de prezentare.

Partea 4: Ghid de Deployment Pas cu Pas

Trei Optiuni de Deployment

  • Optiunea A: Railway (Recomandata) — Cel mai simplu mod de a deploya o aplicatie FastAPI. Detecteaza Dockerfile-ul automat, aloca un server si iti ofera un URL public in sub 5 minute.
  • Optiunea B: Render — Se conecteaza la repository-ul GitHub si face deploy automat la fiecare push.
  • Optiunea C: Vercel + Railway — Frontend static pe Vercel (CDN global), backend FastAPI pe Railway. Mai complex dar performanta maxima.

Lista de Verificare Post-Deployment

  • HTTPS activ (certificat SSL automat)
  • Variabile de mediu setate in dashboard-ul platformei
  • Endpoint-ul /health returneaza 200
  • Monitor de uptime configurat (UptimeRobot)
  • Timpii de raspuns API testati

Partea 5: De la Proiect Personal la Afacere Reala

Monetizare si Marketing

Construirea unui produs grozav este doar jumatate din batalie. Stripe este standardul industrial pentru platile SaaS. Strategia de pret in 4 niveluri functioneaza pentru aproape orice produs SaaS:

  • Gratuit (carligul): Utilizare limitata, fara card de credit necesar.
  • Starter ($9-19/luna): Suficient pentru utilizatori individuali.
  • Pro ($29-79/luna): Pentru utilizatori avansati si echipe mici.
  • Enterprise (pret personalizat): Pentru organizatii cu nevoi specifice.

Canalele de marketing pentru AI SaaS: Product Hunt, Indie Hackers, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, SEO si Reddit. Cerinte legale: Termeni si Conditii, Politica de Confidentialitate, conformitate GDPR.

Partea 6: Ce Vei Construi in Continuare

Cinci Proiecte GenAI SaaS

  1. Generare de Imagini — PixelForge: SaaS text-la-imagine cu controale de stil.
  2. Generare de Video — ClipCraft: SaaS text/imagine-la-video cu procesare asincrona.
  3. Compozitie & Rescriere Text — ProseAI: Rescrie, rezuma, schimba tonul.
  4. Detectie Plagiat & AI — TruthLens: Detecteaza textul copiat si continutul generat de AI.
  5. OCR & Inteligenta Documentelor — DocMind: Extrage text, tabele, date din imagini/PDF-uri.

Fiecare proiect se construieste pe fundatia partajata din aceasta lectie. Poti construi toate 5 sau te poti specializa in cele care se potrivesc pietei tale.

Pregatit sa construiesti? Blocurile de cod de mai jos iti ofera tot ce ai nevoie pentru a incepe: un template de proiect complet, un furnizor AI universal, un exemplu de personalizare, un script de deployment, un template de configurare si un template de pagina de prezentare.

Stathio 6: GenAI SaaS

Vaseis GenAI SaaS: APIs, Prosarmogi & Deployment

To Koino Schedio Pisw apo Kathe Proion AI SaaS pou tha Chtiseis

~45 lepta anagnwsi | Themelio | Apo LLM se SaaS pou paragei esoda

Giati Yparxei ayti i Dialeksi

Exeis ekpaideusi ena Mini GPT-2 apo to miden. Katanoeis ti tokenization, tin prosochi, tous transformers kai to backpropagation. Boreis na parageis keimeno me to diko sou modelo. Auto einai mia aksiosimeiwti epityxia — alla den einai proion. Kaneis den tha plirosei gia ena Python script pou trexei se ena Jupyter notebook.

Ayti i dialeksi gefyronei to xasma metaksy «Exo ena LLM» kai «Exo ena proion SaaS pou paragei esoda.» Sta epomena pente erga, tha chtiseis pente pragmatikes, deployable efarmoges SaaS me AI: dimiourgia eikonon, dimiourgia video, anagraphi keimenou, anixneusi logoklophs kai nohmosyhi eggrafon. Oles moirazontai tin idia architektoniki themeliwsi, to idio pipeline deployment kai tin idia stratigiki nohmatiodoitsis.

Meros 1: I Architektoniki GenAI SaaS

I Stoiva me Tessera Epipeda

Kathe efarmogi SaaS pou tha chtiseis se ayto to mathima akolouthei tin idia architektoniki me tessera epipeda:

  1. Frontend (Statiko HTML/CSS/JS) — Ti vlepei kai me ti allilepidra o xristis. Exipireteitai ws statika arxeia apo ton idio server pou trexei to API.
  2. Epipedo API (FastAPI) — O egkefalos tis efarmogis sou. Lamvanei aitimata, epikyrwnei eisodo, efarmozei oria xrewsis, kalei to AI backend kai epistrefei domomenes apantiseis.
  3. AI Backend — To epipedo noimosynis. Borei na einai to diko sou Mini GPT-2 modelo i ena emporiko API opws OpenAI, Google Gemini i Anthropic Claude.
  4. Apothikeusi & Katastasi — Opou zoun ta monima dedomena. Logariasmoi xriston, egrafes xrewsis, paragomena apotelesmata.

Giati FastAPI?

Epileksame to FastAPI gia kathe ergo se ayto to mathima gia pente sigkekrimenos logous: async by default, aftomati tekmiriosi, asfalia typon, apodosi kai exipiretisi statikon arxeion. To FastAPI diaxeirizetai xiliades tautoxronon aitimatwn enw perimenei apantiseis AI.

I Koini Domi Ergou

my-saas/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py          # Efarmogi FastAPI + routes
│   ├── config.py         # Rythmiseis & metavlites perivallontos
│   ├── billing.py        # Parakolouthisi xrisis & epipeda
│   └── [domain].py       # Logiki sigkekrimenou ergou
├── static/
│   └── index.html        # Diepafi frontend
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
└── .env

Meros 2: Syndesi me ta LLM APIs

Tesseris Tropoi gia na Prostheseis Noimosyni

  • Epilogi A: To diko sou Mini GPT-2 — Miden kostos API, pliros elegxos, alla xamiloteri poiotita.
  • Epilogi B: OpenAI API (GPT-4o-mini) — To pio eyxristo emporiko API. Kostos: ~$0.15/1M tokens eisodou.
  • Epilogi C: Google Gemini API — Eksereti apodosi se xamiloterres times. Kostos: ~$0.075/1M tokens eisodou.
  • Epilogi D: Anthropic Claude API — Leptomeries apantiseis, eksereti akolouthisi odigion. Kostos: ~$0.25/1M tokens eisodou.

I enopoiimeni klasi AIProvider mas afairopoiei tis diafores. Rythmizeis poion paroxi na xrisimopoiiseis mesw tis metavlitis perivallontos AI_PROVIDER. I allagi apo to diko sou modelo se GPT-4o se Gemini apaiti allagi mias monadikis metavlitis perivallontos kai miden grammes kodika efarmogis.

Asfaleia Kleidion API: Min kaneis pote commit kleidia API sto Git. Min ta vazeis sto frontend JavaScript. Fortone ta panta apo metavlites perivallontos ston server.

Meros 2b: Pistopoiisi & Diaxeirisi Xriston

Exeis syndedei tin efarmogi sou me ena LLM API. Borei na paragei keimeno, eikones i na analysei eggrafa. Alla auto ti stigmi, opoiosdipote vrei to URL sou borei na to xrisimopoiisei — kai kathe klisi API sou kostizei xrimata. Prin to proion SaaS sou borei na paragei esoda, prepei na kserei poios to xrisimopoiei, poso to xrisimopoiei kai an exei plirosei gia ayto. Ayto lyni i pistopoiisi kai i diaxeirisi xriston.

Giati Exei Simasia i Pistopoiisi gia ta Proionta SaaS

  • Parakolouthisi xrisis ana xristi: Prepei na kseri poios xristis ekane poia klisi API gia na efarmoseis ta epipeda xrewsis kai ta oria rythmou.
  • Xrewsi gia tin ypiresia sou: I epeksergasia pliromon apaiti mia tautotita xristi gia na syndethei me mia syndromi i methodo plirwmis.
  • Prostasia ton kleidion API sou: Xoris pistopoiisi, ta akriva kleidia OpenAI i Gemini sou einai oysia dimosiaI. Enas kakoithis xristis tha borouse na syssoreusi xiliades dollaria se xrewseis.
  • Prosfora prosopropoiimenon empeirion: Apothikevmenes protimiseis, istoriko kai prosarmosmenes rythmiseis apailtoun oles ena logariasmo xristi.
  • Symorfosi me kanonismous: O GDPR kai alloi nomoi aporritou apailtoun na ksereis tinon dedomena epeksergaeste.

Pistopoiisi me Vasi JWT

Kai ta pente proionta GenAI SaaS se ayto to mathima xrisimopoioun JSON Web Tokens (JWT) gia pistopoiisi. Na pos leitoyrgei:

  1. Syndesi: O xristis stelnei to email kai ton kodiko prosavsais sto endpoint /api/auth/login.
  2. Epivevaiwsi: O server elegxei ta diapisteutiria stin vasi dedomenon.
  3. Dimiourgia token: An einai egkyra, o server dimiourgei ena JWT — ena kryptografika ypogrammeno string pou periexei to ID xristi, email, rolo kai xrono liksis.
  4. Apothikeusi client: To frontend apothikevei ayto to token (synithws se HTTP-only cookie i localStorage).
  5. Epomenes aitiseis: Kathe klisi API perilamvanei to token sto header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  6. Epikyrosi: O server epivevaionei tin ypografi tou token se kathe aitima xoris na prosvali ti vasi dedomenon, kanontasto extretika grigoro.

OAuth2 Koinoniki Syndesi

  • Google OAuth: Oi xristes kanoun klik sto «Syndesi me Google», anakateuthynontai sti selida syndesis tis Google, eksousioditoun tin efarmogi sou kai stelnontai piso me enan kodiko eksousidotisis. O server sou antallassei ayton ton kodiko gia pliroforiers profil (onoma, email, avatar).
  • GitHub OAuth: Idia roi me to Google alla xrisimopoiontas logariasmous GitHub. Idiaitera dimofilis gia ergaleia pou apeuthinontai se programmatistes.

Synkrisi Paroxon Pistopoiisis

Paroxos Dorean Epipedo Times Kalytera Gia
Clerk 10.000 MAU $25/mina (Pro) Omorfa prokataskevamena stoixeia UI, tachyteri egkatastasi
Auth0 7.500 MAU $23/mina (Essentials) Enterprise xaraktiristika, ektetameni prosarmogi
Supabase Auth 50.000 MAU Perilamvanetai me Supabase ($25/mina Pro) Idi xrisimopoieis Supabase gia vasi dedomenon, gennaiodoro dorean epipedo
Firebase Auth Aperioristo (oi perissotera leitourgies) Dorean gia pistopoiisi Oikosystima Google, kinittes efarmoges

Pos Ylopoioun ta Proionta SaaS tin Pistopoiisi

  • app/auth.py — Periexei to middleware pistopoiisis, dimiourgia kai epikyrosi JWT tokens, hashing kodikou prosvasis me bcrypt kai diaxeirisi synedrias xristi. Parexei tin eksartisi get_current_user pou prosthetes se opoiodipote endpoint FastAPI pou apaiti pistopoiisi.
  • app/stripe_checkout.py — Diaxeirizetai ti syndesi metaksy pistopoiisis kai pliromon. Otan enas xristis kanei syndromi, to Stripe stelnei ena webhook ston server sou. Ayto to arxeio epeksergasetai to webhook, enimeronei tin katastasi syndromis kai prosarmozes to epipedo xrewsis.

Periorisi Rythmou kai Diaxeirisi Kleidion API

  • Oria ana xristi: Oi dorean xristes boroun na lovou 10 aitimata tin imera, enw oi Pro xristes lamvanoun 500. To arthro billing.py parakolouthei ti xrisi ana pistopoiimeno xristi.
  • Diaxeirisi kleidion API: Gia xristes pou theloun programmatiki prosvasi, dimiourgise monadika kleidia API syndedemena me ton logariasmo tous. Apothikeve ta kleidia ws hashismenes times sti vasi dedomenon.
  • Pagkosmia perioriasi rythmou: Peran ton orion ana xristi, ylopoiise pagkosmia perioriasi rythmou gia na apotresei tin yperfortosi olokliroi tou systimatos.
  • Parakolouthisi kostous: Katagraphe kathe klisi API me to kostos tis se tokens. Ayta ta dedomena trofoditoun to systima xrewsis kai se voithoun na orizeis times pou kalyptoun ta eksoda sou me ygies perithoris.
Ypenthymisi asfaleias: Min ektheseis pote ta kleidia API tou paroxi AI (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) sto frontend. Oles oi kliseis AI API prepei na pernoun apo to FastAPI backend sou, to opoio prostheti to kleidi API apo tin pleura tou server. O xristis pistopoieitai me tin ypiresia sou; i ypiresia sou pistopoieitai me ton paroxi AI. Dyo xorista epipeda pistopoiisis, kathenam prostatenontas diaforetika diapisteutiria.

Meros 3: Pos na Prosarmosei to SaaS sou

Odigos Vima pros Vima

  1. Branding: Allakse to onoma tis efarmogis, ta xromata, to logo sto index.html.
  2. System Prompts: Tropopoiise ta system prompts gia na tairiazoun sti nixia sou.
  3. Xaraktiristika: Prosthese/afairese endpoints, allakse ta epipeda xrewsis.
  4. Estias se Tomea: Eksoikeiwthi gia ena vertical (nomiko, iatriko, ekpaideutiko, marketing).
  5. White-labeling: Exipiretise kato apo to diko sou domain.

Paradeigma: Metatropi tou generikou «SaaS Anagrafis Keimenou» se «LegalDraft Pro» — ena ergaleio anagrafis nomikon eggrafon.

Meros 4: Odigos Deployment Vima pros Vima

Treis Epiloges Deployment

  • Epilogi A: Railway (Synistomeni) — O aploysteros tropos gia na kaneis deploy mia efarmogi FastAPI. Public URL se ligotero apo 5 lepta.
  • Epilogi B: Render — Syndetai me to GitHub repository kai kanei deploy aftomata se kathe push.
  • Epilogi C: Vercel + Railway — Statiko frontend sto Vercel, FastAPI backend sto Railway. Pio periploko alla megisti apodosi.

Meros 5: Apo Prosopiko Ergo se Pragmatiki Epixeirisi

Nohmatiodoitsi kai Marketing

I stratigiki tis tetraplis timologisis leitourgei gia sxedon kathe proion SaaS:

  • Dorean (to agkistri): Periorismeni xrisi, xoris pistwtiki karta.
  • Starter ($9-19/mina): Arketa gia atomikou xristes.
  • Pro ($29-79/mina): Gia proigmenous xristes kai mikres omades.
  • Enterprise (prosarmosmeni timi): Gia organismos me sigkekrimenes anagkes.

Kanalia marketing gia AI SaaS: Product Hunt, Indie Hackers, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, SEO kai Reddit. Nomikes apaitiseis: Oroi Xrisis, Politiki Aporritou, symmorfowtsi GDPR.

Meros 6: Ti tha Chtiseis Meta

Pente Erga GenAI SaaS

  1. Dimiourgia Eikonon — PixelForge: SaaS text-to-image me elegxous styl.
  2. Dimiourgia Video — ClipCraft: SaaS text/eikona-se-video me asynxroni epeksergasia.
  3. Synthesi & Anagraphi Keimenou — ProseAI: Anagrapsi, perilipsi, allagi tonou.
  4. Anixneusi Logoklophs & AI — TruthLens: Anixneusi antigrafenou kai AI-paragomenou periexomenou.
  5. OCR & Noimosyni Eggrafon — DocMind: Eksagogi keimenou, pinakon, dedomenon apo eikones/PDFs.

Kathe ergo xtizetai pano sti koini themeliwsi apo ayti ti dialeksi. Boreis na chtiseis kai ta 5 i na eksoikeiwtheis se ayta pou tairiazoun stin agora sou.

Etoimos na chtiseis? Ta code blocks parakatw sou dinoun oti xreiazesai gia na ksekinisei: ena plires project template, enan pagkosmio AI provider, ena paradeigma prosarmogis, ena deployment script, ena template rythmiseon kai ena template selidas proorismos.

"""
GenAI SaaS - Shared Project Template (main.py)
=============================================
This is the foundation for every GenAI SaaS project in this course.
Copy this file, modify the domain-specific endpoints, and you have
a deployable AI-powered SaaS application.
"""

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, FileResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel
import os
import time
import logging

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
APP_NAME = os.getenv("APP_NAME", "GenAI SaaS")
APP_VERSION = os.getenv("APP_VERSION", "1.0.0")
ENVIRONMENT = os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT", "development")
ALLOWED_ORIGINS = os.getenv("ALLOWED_ORIGINS", "*").split(",")

# ── Logging Setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
)
logger = logging.getLogger(APP_NAME)

# ── FastAPI App ────────────────────────────────────────────────
app = FastAPI(
    title=APP_NAME,
    version=APP_VERSION,
    description=f"{APP_NAME} - AI-Powered SaaS Application",
    docs_url="/docs" if ENVIRONMENT == "development" else None,
    redoc_url=None,
)

# ── CORS Middleware ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Required for frontend-backend communication
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# ── Request Logging Middleware ─────────────────────────────────
@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    start_time = time.time()
    response = await call_next(request)
    duration = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(
        f"{request.method} {request.url.path} "
        f"- {response.status_code} - {duration:.3f}s"
    )
    return response

# ── Global Exception Handler ──────────────────────────────────
@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def global_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception):
    logger.error(f"Unhandled exception: {exc}", exc_info=True)
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=500,
        content={
            "error": "Internal server error",
            "message": str(exc) if ENVIRONMENT == "development" else
                       "Something went wrong. Please try again.",
        },
    )

# ── Health Check ───────────────────────────────────────────────
@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    """Health check endpoint for monitoring services."""
    return {
        "status": "healthy",
        "app": APP_NAME,
        "version": APP_VERSION,
        "environment": ENVIRONMENT,
        "timestamp": time.time(),
    }

# ── API Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
@app.get("/api/info")
async def api_info():
    """Return API metadata and available endpoints."""
    return {
        "app": APP_NAME,
        "version": APP_VERSION,
        "endpoints": {
            "health": "/health",
            "docs": "/docs",
            "api_info": "/api/info",
        },
    }

# ── Request/Response Models ────────────────────────────────────
# Define your domain-specific models here
class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str

Unified AI Provider
===================
One class, four backends: Own Model, OpenAI, Gemini, Claude.
Switch between them with a single environment variable.

In Pyodide (browser), runs in demo mode with simulated responses.
"""

import os
import json
import time

# ── Detect if running in Pyodide (browser) ────────────────────
try:
    import pyodide  # noqa: F401
    IN_PYODIDE = True
except ImportError:
    IN_PYODIDE = False


class AIProvider:
    """
    Unified AI provider that supports 4 backends:
    - "own"      → Your Mini GPT-2 model (local inference)
    - "openai"   → OpenAI API (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o)
    - "gemini"   → Google Gemini API (Flash, Pro)
    - "claude"   → Anthropic Claude API (Haiku, Sonnet)
    - "demo"     → Simulated responses (for testing/Pyodide)
    """

    def __init__(self):
        if IN_PYODIDE:
            self.provider = "demo"
            self.model = "demo-mode"
            print("[AIProvider] Running in Pyodide → demo mode")
        else:
            self.provider = os.getenv("AI_PROVIDER", "demo").lower()
            self.model = os.getenv("AI_MODEL", self._default_model())
            print(f"[AIProvider] Provider: {self.provider}, Model: {self.model}")

    def _default_model(self):
        defaults = {
            "own": "mini-gpt2",
            "openai": "gpt-4o-mini",
            "gemini": "gemini-1.5-flash",
            "claude": "claude-3-haiku-20240307",
            "demo": "demo-mode",
        }
        return defaults.get(self.provider, "demo-mode")

    async def generate(self, prompt: str, system_prompt: str = "",
                       max_tokens: int = 500, temperature: float = 0.7) -> dict:
        """Generate text using the configured AI provider."""
        start = time.time()

        method = {
            "own": self._generate_own,
            "openai": self._generate_openai,
            "gemini": self._generate_gemini,
            "claude": self._generate_claude,
            "demo": self._generate_demo,
        }.get(self.provider, self._generate_demo)

        result = await method(prompt, system_prompt, max_tokens, temperature)
        result["processing_time"] = round(time.time() - start, 3)
        result["provider"] = self.provider
        result["model"] = self.model
        return result

    # ── Own Model (Mini GPT-2) ─────────────────────────────────
    async def _generate_own(self, prompt, system_prompt, max_tokens, temperature):
        """Load and run your own Mini GPT-2 model."""
        # Import your model from the training lectures
        # from your_model import MiniGPT2, generate_text
        # model = MiniGPT2.load("checkpoints/mini_gpt2.pt")
        # text = generate_text(model, prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens)
        return {
            "text": f"[Own Model] Would generate from: {prompt[:50]}...",
            "tokens_used": max_tokens,
            "note": "Replace with actual model loading code"
        }

    # ── OpenAI ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    async def _generate_openai(self, prompt, system_prompt, max_tokens, temperature):
        """Call OpenAI Chat Completions API."""
        import httpx

        api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
        if not api_key:
            raise ValueError("OPENAI_API_KEY not set in environment")

        messages = []
        if system_prompt:
            messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system_prompt})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})

        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
            response = await client.post(
                "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions",
                headers={
                    "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                },
                json={
                    "model": self.model,
                    "messages": messages,
                    "max_tokens": max_tokens,
                    "temperature": temperature,
                },
                timeout=30.0,
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()

        return {
            "text": data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"],
            "tokens_used": data["usage"]["total_tokens"],
        }

    # ── Google Gemini ──────────────────────────────────────────
    async def _generate_gemini(self, prompt, system_prompt, max_tokens, temperature):
        """Call Google Gemini generateContent API."""
        import httpx

        api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")
        if not api_key:
            raise ValueError("GEMINI_API_KEY not set in environment")

        full_prompt = f"{system_prompt}\n\n{prompt}" if system_prompt else prompt

        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
            response = await client.post(
                f"https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/"
                f"{self.model}:generateContent?key={api_key}",
                json={
                    "contents": [{"parts": [{"text": full_prompt}]}],
                    "generationConfig": {
                        "maxOutputTokens": max_tokens,
                        "temperature": temperature,
                    },
                },
                timeout=30.0,
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()

        text = data["candidates"][0]["content"]["parts"][0]["text"]
        tokens = data.get("usageMetadata", {}).get("totalTokenCount", 0)

        return {"text": text, "tokens_used": tokens}

    # ── Anthropic Claude ───────────────────────────────────────
    async def _generate_claude(self, prompt, system_prompt, max_tokens, temperature):
        """Call Anthropic Messages API."""
        import httpx

        api_key = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        if not api_key:
            raise ValueError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set in environment")

        body = {
            "model": self.model,
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "temperature": temperature,
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        }
        if system_prompt:
            body["system"] = system_prompt

        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
            response = await client.post(
                "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages",
                headers={
                    "x-api-key": api_key,
                    "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                },
                json=body,
                timeout=30.0,
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()

        text = data["content"][0]["text"]
        tokens = data["usage"]["input_tokens"] + data["usage"]["output_tokens"]

        return {"text": text, "tokens_used": tokens}

    # ── Demo Mode ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    async def _generate_demo(self, prompt, system_prompt, max_tokens, temperature):
        """Simulated responses for testing and Pyodide."""
        import random

        demo_responses = [
            f"This is a demo response to your prompt about: {prompt[:80]}",
            f"In demo mode, I would process: '{prompt[:60]}...' with the "
            f"system context: '{system_prompt[:40]}...'",
            f"[Demo] AI analysis of your input suggests the following key "
            f"themes: {', '.join(prompt.split()[:5])}",
        ]
        return {
            "text": random.choice(demo_responses),
            "tokens_used": len(prompt.split()) + max_tokens // 4,
        }


# ── Quick Test ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

async def main():

    result = await provider.generate(

        system_prompt="You are a helpful science teacher.",

    )
    print(f"\nProvider: {result['provider']}")
    print(f"Model:    {result['model']}")
    print(f"Tokens:   {result['tokens_used']}")
    print(f"Time:     {result['processing_time']}s")
    print(f"Response: {result['text']}")

asyncio.run(main())
